documents.title: Terms of Service
documents.summary: The agreement between Smartline Publishers and the organisation that uses SmartOS to manage its publishing operations.

content.changelog: Version 1.0 - initial published version aligned with the SmartOS registration and invitation flows.
reviewFlags: Confirm the full legal entity name, company registration number, registered address and contact email that must appear in the contract and notices.
Confirm the governing law, exclusive venue and whether arbitration or consumer-dispute rules apply in the operating jurisdictions.
Confirm commercial terms: plan pricing, taxes, invoicing, renewal, cancellation, refunds and any service-level commitments.
Confirm the liability cap basis (fees paid in the preceding 12 months or another amount) and any non-excludable liability wording with counsel.
Confirm the minimum age for account holders and whether additional terms are needed for authors, contractors or minors.

sections.heading: 1. Who we are and what these terms cover
paragraphs: SmartOS is publishing-operations software operated by Smartline Publishers ("Smartline", "we", "us"). It brings catalogue, editorial, production, inventory, sales, finance and royalty workflows into one organisation workspace.

These Terms of Service ("Terms") form a binding agreement between Smartline and the organisation that creates or uses a SmartOS workspace ("Customer", "you"). They apply to the organisation's administrators and to every user it invites.

Smartline provides the software only. We are not your publisher, literary agent, distributor, accountant, tax adviser or legal adviser, and we do not acquire rights in the books, manuscripts or other content you manage in SmartOS.
reviewFlags: Replace "Smartline Publishers" with the contracting legal entity and add its registration details.

sections.heading: 2. Accounts, authority and workspace access
paragraphs: The first person who creates a workspace becomes its organisation administrator. That administrator is responsible for configuring the workspace and for deciding which colleagues, authors, contractors or service providers receive access.

By creating a workspace or accepting an invitation, you confirm that you are at least the minimum age stated in these Terms, that you have authority to bind the organisation (or that the administrator has authorised your access), and that the information you provide is accurate.

You must keep credentials and passkeys secure, enable a second factor where appropriate, and tell us promptly if you believe an account has been compromised. Actions taken through an authenticated account are treated as authorised by the organisation unless you have notified us of a compromise.
We may suspend an account or session to protect the service, investigate suspected misuse, comply with law, or enforce plan limits. Where practicable, we will tell the organisation why.
reviewFlags: Confirm the minimum age (for example 18, or 16 with guardian consent) and insert it here.

sections.heading: 3. Your workspace and your content
paragraphs: As between Smartline and the Customer, the Customer owns all data it submits to SmartOS, including organisation details, book and manuscript records, contributor and customer information, orders, stock movements, finance entries and royalty statements ("Customer Data").

You grant Smartline a limited, non-exclusive licence to host, copy, process, transmit and display Customer Data only as needed to provide, secure, support and improve the service, or as instructed by the organisation.

You are responsible for the lawfulness, accuracy and quality of Customer Data. This includes having a lawful basis to store personal data about authors, customers, employees and other individuals, and having the rights needed to upload manuscripts, cover artwork and other files.
Workspaces are logically isolated by organisation. You must not attempt to access another organisation's data, and you must tell us if you believe isolation has failed.

sections.heading: 4. Acceptable use
paragraphs: You must use SmartOS lawfully and only for legitimate publishing operations. The following are not permitted:
bullets: Uploading or sharing content that infringes copyright, trade marks, privacy, confidence or other rights, or that is defamatory, fraudulent, abusive, exploitative or unlawful.
Publishing or distributing material that sexualises minors, incites violence or hatred, or facilitates crime.
Attempting to gain unauthorised access to an account, workspace, network or system, probing or scanning the service, or bypassing authentication, permissions or plan limits.
Introducing malware, ransomware, worms or other harmful code, or using the service to deliver spam or phishing.
Scraping, crawling or bulk-extracting data without written permission, or using automated means that materially burden the service.
Reverse engineering, decompiling or copying the software except to the extent that law expressly permits it, or reselling or white-labelling the service without a written agreement.
Using SmartOS to make automated decisions about individuals that produce legal or similarly significant effects without appropriate human review.

sections.heading: 5. Publishing, financial and royalty records are your responsibility
paragraphs: SmartOS records and calculates from the information your team enters. Print-run availability, stock deductions, order totals, royalties, budgets and financial summaries are only as reliable as the underlying data and configuration.

You are responsible for author contracts, rights grants, royalty rates, reserve and returns policies, taxes, statutory reporting and payments to authors and other rights holders. SmartOS does not provide legal, tax, accounting or investment advice.

Once a print run is posted, its stock effect is treated as final. Corrections must be made through an adjustment with an audit trail, not by rewriting history. You are responsible for reviewing adjustments and for reconciling SmartOS records with your accounting and warehouse systems.

sections.heading: 6. Plans, fees, limits and billing
paragraphs: SmartOS is offered on the plans displayed in the product or an order form. Plans differ in user, book and feature limits. The limits shown in the product at the time of purchase apply.

Unless an order form says otherwise, fees are payable in advance, are stated exclusive of applicable taxes, and are non-refundable except where law requires a refund or where we terminate for our own convenience.

We may change plan limits or prices for a future billing period by giving reasonable notice. If you do not agree, you may stop using the service before the change takes effect. Overdue amounts may lead to suspension after notice.
The billing module currently records plan information and payment status; it does not by itself create a payment obligation beyond the plan selected by the organisation.
reviewFlags: Confirm prices, currency, tax treatment, invoicing cycle, renewal and refund policy, and whether a payment processor is used.

sections.heading: 7. Availability, changes and support
paragraphs: We work to keep SmartOS available and secure, but the service is provided on an "as available" basis unless a separate written service-level agreement applies. Maintenance, upgrades, third-party outages and events outside our reasonable control may interrupt access.

We may add, change or retire features. We will give reasonable notice of material changes that adversely affect core workflows. Features marked beta or preview may change or be withdrawn without notice and should not be relied on for irreversible business records.

Support is provided through the channels identified in the Help centre. Include the workspace, affected record and steps to reproduce so we can investigate. Response times are targets, not guaranteed deadlines, unless a separate support agreement says otherwise.
reviewFlags: Confirm support hours, channels, response targets and whether any uptime commitment or service credits apply.

sections.heading: 8. Intellectual property
paragraphs: Smartline and its licensors own the SmartOS software, design system, documentation, trade marks and all improvements to them. These Terms grant a limited, revocable, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the service during the subscription, subject to these Terms.

The Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and of its own brand assets. The Customer grants Smartline permission to use its name and logo only as needed to provide the service or, with written consent, in a customer list.

If you send feedback or suggestions, you grant us a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use them to improve the service, without any obligation to compensate you or to treat the feedback as confidential.

sections.heading: 9. Confidentiality
paragraphs: Each party may receive information that the other treats as confidential, including unpublished manuscripts, pricing and business plans. The receiving party must use it only for the purpose of the agreement and protect it with reasonable care.

Confidentiality does not apply to information that is public through no breach, independently developed, lawfully received from a third party, or required to be disclosed by law or a competent authority. Where lawful, we will give prompt notice of a compelled disclosure.
These obligations survive termination for as long as the information remains confidential.

sections.heading: 10. Data protection
paragraphs: Our Privacy Policy explains what personal data we collect, why, how long we keep it and the rights available to individuals. It forms part of these Terms.

For personal data inside a Customer workspace, the Customer is generally the controller and Smartline acts as processor. Where required, the parties will enter a data processing agreement covering instructions, subprocessors, security, breach assistance, deletion and audits.
You must not use SmartOS to process special-category data or other high-risk data unless you have assessed the risk and put appropriate safeguards in place.
reviewFlags: Confirm whether a separate data processing agreement is required and prepare a subprocessor list.

sections.heading: 11. Suspension, termination and data export
paragraphs: You may stop using SmartOS at any time. We may suspend or terminate access if you materially breach these Terms, fail to pay undisputed fees after notice, create a security or legal risk, or if required by law.

On termination, the organisation's administrator may request an export of Customer Data within the period stated in the Privacy Policy. After that period we may delete or anonymise the data, subject to backups, legal holds and records we must retain.
We may also terminate the service generally by giving reasonable notice. In that case we will provide a practical export window and a pro-rata refund of prepaid, unused fees where appropriate.
Provisions that by their nature should survive termination - including ownership, confidentiality, disclaimers, liability and governing law - continue to apply.
reviewFlags: Confirm the post-termination export window and deletion period.

sections.heading: 12. Disclaimers and limitation of liability
paragraphs: To the maximum extent permitted by law, SmartOS is provided without implied warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, non-infringement or uninterrupted error-free operation. We do not warrant that reports, royalty calculations or stock balances will be free of errors caused by incomplete or incorrect input.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, or for lost profits, lost revenue, lost goodwill or loss of data, even if advised of the possibility.

Subject to the paragraph below, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to these Terms is limited to the fees paid or payable by the Customer for SmartOS in the twelve months before the event giving rise to the claim.

Nothing in these Terms excludes or limits liability that cannot lawfully be excluded, including liability for fraud, wilful misconduct, death or personal injury caused by negligence, or any mandatory consumer rights.
reviewFlags: Confirm the liability cap and any carve-outs with counsel, especially for data-protection breaches.

sections.heading: 13. Indemnity
paragraphs: To the extent permitted by law, the Customer will defend and indemnify Smartline against third-party claims, losses and reasonable costs arising from Customer Data, content the Customer uploads or distributes, or the Customer's breach of these Terms or applicable law.

Smartline will defend and indemnify the Customer against third-party claims that the SmartOS software itself infringes a valid intellectual-property right, provided the Customer promptly notifies us and allows us to control the defence. This does not apply to claims caused by Customer Data, modifications or use outside these Terms.

sections.heading: 14. Governing law and disputes
paragraphs: These Terms are governed by the laws of the jurisdiction stated in the review note below, without regard to conflict-of-law rules. The courts or arbitral tribunal of that jurisdiction have exclusive jurisdiction, except that either party may seek urgent injunctive relief in any competent court.
Before starting formal proceedings, the parties will try in good faith to resolve a dispute through the organisation administrator and Smartline support for at least 30 days.
Nothing in this section prevents an individual from bringing a claim in a court that mandatory consumer law makes available to them.
reviewFlags: Insert the governing law and venue, and confirm whether arbitration, mediation or small-claims rules apply.

sections.heading: 15. Changes to these Terms
paragraphs: We may update these Terms to reflect changes in the service, law, security practice or commercial model. Each published version has a version number and effective date.

If a change materially affects your rights or obligations, we will give reasonable notice in the product or by email. Where required, we will ask the organisation administrator to accept the new version before continuing to use the affected features.
Acceptance is recorded with the user, organisation, document version and timestamp so both parties can verify which terms applied.

sections.heading: 16. Contact and notices
paragraphs: Legal notices to Smartline must be sent to the contact address below. Notices to the Customer may be sent to the organisation administrator's email address or shown in the product.
For support questions, use the Help centre rather than the legal contact. For privacy requests, follow the process in the Privacy Policy.
reviewFlags: Insert the legal entity name, registered address, legal email and any required company registration or VAT details.

documents.title: Privacy Policy
documents.summary: How Smartline Publishers handles personal data when providing SmartOS, including account data, workspace records, security logs and support conversations.

content.changelog: Version 1.0 - initial published version aligned with the SmartOS registration and invitation flows.
reviewFlags: Confirm the identity of the data controller and processor, the registered address and the privacy contact or Data Protection Officer.
Confirm hosting region, international-transfer mechanism (for example SCCs or an adequacy decision) and all subprocessors.
Confirm retention periods for accounts, workspace data, audit logs, backups and support records.
Confirm whether cookie analytics, product analytics, error monitoring or marketing tools are enabled, and update the cookies section accordingly.
Confirm the competent supervisory authority and the breach-notification process.

sections.heading: 1. Scope and who is responsible
paragraphs: This Privacy Policy explains how Smartline Publishers ("Smartline", "we", "us") collects, uses, shares, stores and protects personal data in connection with SmartOS, our websites, support channels and related communications.

There are two roles. For account, billing, security and relationship data about the organisation and its users, Smartline is the controller. For personal data that an organisation stores inside its workspace - for example author, customer, employee or contractor records - the organisation is normally the controller and Smartline acts as its processor.

If you are a member of an organisation's workspace, the organisation decides what data is entered and who can see it. Contact that organisation first for requests about workspace data; we will assist it as required by our agreement.
reviewFlags: Insert the controller's legal entity name, address and privacy contact.

sections.heading: 2. Personal data we collect
paragraphs: We collect the following categories of personal data:
bullets: Account and identity data: name, email address, password hash, organisation name and slug, role, avatar, passkey metadata, two-factor status and invitation status.
Authentication and security data: session and refresh-token records, IP address, user agent, login timestamps, failed-attempt counters, password-change history and audit events.

Workspace data: records your organisation chooses to enter, such as contributor and customer contact details, author contracts, tasks, orders, stock movements, finance entries, royalty statements and uploaded files.
Support and communications: messages, attachments and contact details you send when asking for help or exercising a right.

Billing and plan data: plan, user and book limits, billing status and any invoice or payment references. Card details, if collected at all, are handled by a payment processor rather than stored in SmartOS.

Technical and usage data: pages and actions used, device and browser information, error diagnostics and approximate location derived from IP address. Analytics is only enabled if the deployment is configured for it.
reviewFlags: Confirm whether product analytics, error monitoring or marketing cookies are enabled and add the exact tools here.

sections.heading: 3. Why we use personal data and our legal bases
paragraphs: We use personal data to create and secure accounts, provide the workspace, enforce plan limits, process invitations, send service messages, provide support, maintain audit records, prevent abuse and improve reliability.

Under the UK/EU GDPR and similar laws, our legal bases are: performance of a contract (providing SmartOS to the organisation); legitimate interests (security, fraud prevention, service improvement and business administration); legal obligation (tax, accounting and lawful requests); and consent where we ask for it (for example optional analytics or marketing).

We do not sell personal data. We do not use workspace content to train third-party advertising models. We may use aggregated or de-identified information that cannot reasonably identify an individual to understand product usage and improve the service.

Where the organisation is the controller, it is responsible for identifying its own legal bases for the personal data it enters. Smartline processes that data on the organisation's documented instructions.

sections.heading: 4. Sensitive data and children
paragraphs: SmartOS is designed for publishing operations, not for special-category data such as health, biometric, political or religious information. Do not enter such data unless you have a lawful basis and appropriate safeguards.

SmartOS is a business tool for authorised adults. It is not directed at children, and we do not knowingly create accounts for children. If you believe a child has provided personal data, contact us and we will investigate and delete it where appropriate.
Some workspace records may relate to minors, for example a young author or a customer's family account. The organisation is responsible for obtaining any required consent and for limiting access.
reviewFlags: Confirm the minimum age and the process for handling suspected underage accounts.

sections.heading: 5. Sharing and subprocessors
paragraphs: We share personal data only as needed to run SmartOS:
bullets: Hosting and database providers that store the application and its PostgreSQL database.
Email delivery providers used for invitations, password resets and service notices.
Image and file storage providers used for avatars, logos and uploaded media.
Error monitoring and support tooling that help us diagnose faults and answer requests.
Payment and billing providers, if paid plans are enabled, to process invoices and payments.
Professional advisers, auditors and insurers under confidentiality obligations.
Authorities, courts or counterparties where required by law or to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.
A successor entity in a merger, acquisition or reorganisation, subject to equivalent protection.
reviewFlags: Replace this list with the actual subprocessors, their purposes and locations, and publish a subprocessor change process.

sections.heading: 6. International transfers
paragraphs: SmartOS may be hosted in a region chosen for the deployment. Some subprocessors may process data in other countries. Where data leaves the UK, EEA or another jurisdiction with transfer restrictions, we use an approved mechanism such as an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses, together with supplementary safeguards where needed.
You can ask the organisation administrator or our privacy contact for more information about the transfer mechanism that applies to your data.
reviewFlags: Confirm the actual hosting region and the transfer mechanism used for each subprocessor.

sections.heading: 7. How long we keep data
paragraphs: We keep personal data only for as long as needed for the purposes described above, including to provide the service, meet legal and accounting obligations, resolve disputes and enforce agreements.

Typical retention: account and workspace data for the life of the organisation plus the post-termination export/backup period; authentication and security records for a limited period sufficient to investigate incidents; audit and legal-acceptance records for as long as needed to demonstrate compliance; support records for a reasonable period after the issue is closed.

When data is no longer needed, we delete it or anonymise it. Backup copies may persist for a limited rotation period before they are overwritten. Legal holds and mandatory retention can extend these periods.
reviewFlags: Insert specific retention periods for accounts, workspace data, audit logs, backups and support tickets.

sections.heading: 8. How we protect data
paragraphs: We use technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, including transport encryption, password hashing with bcrypt, hashed refresh and reset tokens, role-based permissions, organisation-level tenant isolation, rate limiting, audit logging, least-privilege access and secure development practices.

No system is completely secure. You are responsible for keeping credentials and passkeys safe, enabling two-factor authentication where appropriate, and telling us promptly about suspected compromise.

If we become aware of a personal-data breach, we will investigate, contain it and notify affected controllers and regulators where required by law. Organisation administrators should include a security contact so we can reach them quickly.

sections.heading: 9. Your rights
paragraphs: Subject to applicable law, individuals may have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict or object to processing, receive a portable copy of their data, and withdraw consent. Where we process as a controller, you can exercise these rights through the privacy contact below.

We may need to verify your identity before acting. We will respond within the period required by law. If your request concerns workspace data, we may direct you to the organisation that controls it and assist that organisation as needed.
You also have the right to complain to a supervisory authority. We would appreciate the chance to resolve your concern first.
reviewFlags: Insert the competent supervisory authority and the internal escalation contact.

sections.heading: 10. Data controlled by your organisation
paragraphs: Your organisation decides what workspace data to collect, who can access it, how long it keeps it and whether to export or delete it. Smartline staff access workspace data only when needed to provide support, investigate security issues, comply with law or follow the organisation's instructions.
If you leave an organisation, its administrator controls your workspace account and records. You may ask the organisation to update or delete your data. We will assist the organisation in responding.
Organisation administrators can request an export or deletion of workspace data subject to the agreement and applicable retention obligations.

sections.heading: 11. Cookies and local storage
paragraphs: SmartOS uses browser storage that is necessary to operate the service: access and refresh tokens, the selected theme, sidebar preference and similar interface settings. These are not used for advertising.
If optional analytics or error monitoring is enabled in a deployment, it may set additional identifiers or cookies. Where consent is required, the deployment must ask for it before those tools load.
You can clear local storage and cookies in your browser, but doing so will sign you out and reset interface preferences.
reviewFlags: Confirm whether any analytics or marketing cookies are used and, if so, add a consent mechanism and cookie table.

sections.heading: 12. Automated decisions and calculations
paragraphs: SmartOS performs deterministic calculations such as order totals, stock balances, budget summaries and royalty statements. These are record-keeping calculations based on data entered by your team; they are not solely automated decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects about an individual.
Your organisation remains responsible for reviewing calculations and for making decisions about contracts, payments, credit and employment with appropriate human involvement.
We do not use workspace content for automated profiling or advertising.

sections.heading: 13. Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy to reflect changes in our processing, the service, technology or law. Each version has a version number and effective date.

If a change materially affects how we use personal data, we will give reasonable notice and, where required, ask users to accept the new version. Acceptance is recorded with the user, organisation, document version and timestamp.
The current version is always available on the public Legal page.

sections.heading: 14. Contact us
paragraphs: For privacy questions, requests or complaints, contact the privacy team using the details below. Include your name, organisation, the right you are exercising and enough information for us to identify the relevant records.
If you are a workspace user, you can also raise the request with your organisation administrator, who controls the workspace data.
We will acknowledge your request and explain any verification steps or lawful exceptions that apply.
reviewFlags: Insert the privacy email, postal address, Data Protection Officer details (if appointed) and expected response times.
